rulings.docket_item: Cluster-adoption proposal from the c19 rulings (peer_c19.json, rows P09-005/P09-006, spans Prov.20.5-Prov.20.5 and Prov.20.6-Prov.20.6): the same-verse doubling construction (bare noun plus waw-prefixed second instance in ONE verse) occurs in exactly 2 of 915 verses book-wide -- both being this adjacent pair -- and both rows rejected the merge by testing the wrong object (the generic bare noun / contiguous substring). Re-derive the construction sweep word-bound and waw-aware, then adopt the merge into one proverb_cluster row Prov.20.5-Prov.20.6 or decline with a corrected-rival disclosure cure, weighed against the B-2 carriage standard.
rulings.decision: ADOPT the merge: P09-005 and P09-006 are replaced by one proverb_cluster row spanning Prov.20.5-Prov.20.6.
rulings.grounds: The B-2 carriage standard applied to this seam's bytes, every digit re-derived. OBJECT NAMED per allography and tokenization discipline: whitespace-token equality over the consonantal_index.json skeletons (word-bound exact tokens, verse-count unit, 915 verses; the staged extract serializes maqaf as space book-wide, so construct pairs tokenize separately -- the same convention the peer used), never the contiguous-substring mode of sweep.py --skel. Digits: word-bound bare token איש (skeleton) = 53 of 915 verses; word-bound waw-prefixed token ואיש (skeleton) = 14 of 915 (new control digit); contiguous-substring איש = 87 of 915 -- the looser object both primaries cited, a contained-substring figure that is NOT citation-grade for this question; SAME-VERSE co-occurrence of the word-bound bare token WITH the word-bound waw-prefixed token = EXACTLY 2 of 915 verses book-wide: Prov.20.5 and Prov.20.6 -- precisely the pair under review, adjacency computed over the sorted hit list (trivially its sole adjacent pair, the full hit set BEING the pair); the only other same-verse doubling of the noun in ANY shape is the double-bare form at Prov.29.9 (1 of 915, no waw), so the bare-plus-waw doubling construction is book-EXCLUSIVE to this seam. All overlapping digits match peer_c19's re-derivation exactly (53 / 87 / 2). Limb (i), distributional marking: satisfied at B-2's own carrying digit -- 2 of 915 with the seam as sole adjacent pair is maximal rarity for a named, word-bound object. Limb (ii), structural binding: satisfied by a shared construction template in the same syntactic slot, byte-derived at the accent tier (U+0591 ETNAHTA): etnahta falls on word 5 of 8 in Prov.20.5 (אִ֑ישׁ) and word 5 of 9 in Prov.20.6 (חַסְדּ֑וֹ), and in BOTH verses the waw-instance is the FIRST word after the etnahta -- colon-2-initial: וְאִ֖ישׁ תְּבוּנָ֣ה (20:5, words 6-7) and וְאִ֥ישׁ אֱ֝מוּנִ֗ים (20:6, words 6-7), byte-spliced -- each in construct with an abstract quality noun (understanding / faithfulness; no morphology layer is staged, so the construct reading is argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings), each heading the colon that predicates the RARE qualified man against colon 1's ordinary-man material carrying the bare form, and each colon closing on a seek-or-extract predicate: verse-final יִדְלֶֽנָּה (20:5) and מִ֣י יִמְצָֽא (20:6) -- “but a man of understanding will draw it out.” (web:Prov.20.5) / “but who can find a faithful man?” (web:Prov.20.6). The doubled word pair is identical at skeleton and accent-stripped tiers in both verses; the pointed forms differ only in accent placement (אִ֑ישׁ / אִ֣ישׁ; וְאִ֖ישׁ / וְאִ֥ישׁ). Section 6's cluster-evidence list names construction runs (consecutive tov-min sayings) as qualifying C2 cohesion -- a 2-verse run of a book-exclusive construction is that named class at maximal rarity, wording-and-construction glue, not theme-alone. PRECEDENT ALIGNMENT: B-2 adopted at 2 of 915 plus a repeated predication template; B-3 declined a 10 of 915 sole-adjacent-pair token in divergent slots with NO template; B-4 declined failing both limbs. This seam carries B-2's digit AND a slot-parallel template -- the evidence carries the cluster rather than merely permitting it. DECISION LOGIC: both rows' rejected_alternative fields denied the merge by testing the wrong object (P09-005: the noun 'recurs so often through the surrounding sayings'; P09-006: 'a generic term repeated across the surrounding chapters'), challenges already upheld high by peer_c19 with the correct object named; a corrected-rival disclosure cure would have to refute the link as ambient collection vocabulary, and no byte ground refutes a book-exclusive same-construction adjacent pair as ambient (2 of 915 is the opposite of stock). Disclosed divergence, which survives as intra-cluster texture exactly as B-2's distinct scenario imagery does: the BARE instances occupy different slots (colon-1-final genitive of בְלֶב under the etnahta at 20:5 vs mid-colon-1 distributive subject at 20:6) and the members' images differ (deep-water counsel vs claimed loyalty). Outer seams re-derived clean: zero shared skeleton content tokens across Prov.20.4|Prov.20.5 and across Prov.20.6|Prov.20.7; the marks inventory carries NO PE/SAMEKH anywhere in chapter 20 and zero K/Q notes at either member verse, so no span-relevant mark disclosure attaches.

consequence.spec: Author wave: retire P09-005 and P09-006; author ONE replacement row -- span Prov.20.5-Prov.20.6, unit_type proverb_cluster, parent_collection 'C2 Prov.10.1-Prov.22.16'. Tiling is preserved: P09-004 ends at Prov.20.4-Prov.20.4 and P09-007 begins at Prov.20.7-Prov.20.7 (verified from the combined corpus). The merged rationale must NAME the carrying evidence with objects and digits: same-verse word-bound doubling (bare איש plus waw-prefixed ואיש, skeleton, whitespace-token equality) = 2 of 915 verses book-wide, both members of this pair; the superseded looser objects disclosed alongside (word-bound bare 53 of 915; contiguous-substring 87 of 915); the colon geometry (etnahta word 5 in both members; waw-instance colon-2-initial in both, in construct with an abstract quality noun, closing on יִדְלֶֽנָּה / מִ֣י יִמְצָֽא). device_notes records the intra-cluster texture: divergent bare-instance slots, distinct images (deep-water counsel vs claimed loyalty), and the retired rows' synthetic/antithetic couplet textures. The driver swap re-opens the dependent fields per the standing rule: rejected_alternative (now rejecting the two-singles reading on the construction-exclusivity digits), observed_substrate_signals, unit_type, confidence (author re-sets on the corrected evidence). boundary_evidence_refs: web:Prov.20.4 and web:Prov.20.7 (the new outer neighbors, both sharing zero skeleton content tokens with the members) plus oshb refs for both member verses. peer_c19's P09-005/P09-006 work orders (rewrite each rejected_alternative to name the construction and the 2-of-915 digit) are SUPERSEDED -- their substance is absorbed into the merged rationale. Cure tests: (1) re-run the word-bound same-verse co-occurrence sweep (whitespace-token equality against consonantal_index.json, NOT sweep.py --skel substring mode) and confirm it returns exactly {Prov.20.5, Prov.20.6} -- the test that exposed the original defect; (2) re-derive the U+0591 etnahta positions in both spliced verses (word 5 of 8; word 5 of 9) and confirm the colon claims in the revised prose; (3) check_tiling.py over Prov.20.1-Prov.20.30 reports 0 gaps/overlaps with the merged row installed; (4) citation_sweep.py, check_refs_mirror.py, check_universals.py, check_marks.py GREEN on the new row; (5) every Hebrew run byte-collated via collate.py, spliced from verse_map_oshb.json, never re-keyed.

rulings.docket_item: Vocabulary reading from the c21 rulings (peer_c21.json, row P10-005, span Prov.22.28-Prov.22.28, C3): Section 6 names admonition_unit for C3 and grants 'admonition_unit/single_proverb per bytes' only for C4; the row is typed single_proverb. Decide the controlled-vocabulary reading: (a) C3 rows may use single_proverb where a saying genuinely stands alone (the C4 clause as the general sentence-literature principle; row label correct, strategy C3 line the imprecision; amendment queued, no row change), or (b) the letter binds -- C3 is admonition_unit-only and the row needs a label cure. An application of the owner's closed 8-value vocabulary either way.
rulings.decision: SPLIT ruling, one outcome: as COLLECTION LAW, reading (a)'s premise holds -- Section 6 legislates exclusivity only where it says so, and the C3 line names the collection's OPERATIVE category rather than an exclusive grant -- but reading (a)'s row-level conclusion fails on this row's bytes: Prov.22.28 does not stand outside the imperative frame, it IS one, so the label is wrong under EITHER reading. The unit_type change single_proverb -> admonition_unit is ADOPTED (peer_c21's remedy affirmed in outcome, its grounds corrected and its cure test revised), with a bounded mood-test symmetry sweep over the C3 rows and a Section 6 clarifying amendment queued for book close. Not an owner_escalation.
rulings.grounds: (1) The law's own letter, read whole: Section 6 marks binding modal force explicitly where it intends it -- the C2+C5 line carries 'SINGLE_PROVERB DEFAULT' and 'proverb_cluster ONLY'; C7/C8 carry 'likely ONE unit' / 'ONE row' -- while the C3 and C4 lines name categories with descriptive parentheticals, in a section that elsewhere uses expectation-register language ('likely', a parenthesized question mark at 3:13-20). Inflating the C3 line into an exclusivity ban inserts an ONLY the owner did not write, and it proves too much: the shipped C3 corpus carries 10 of 33 rows outside admonition_unit (census re-derived from the combined corpus: 5 single_proverb, 4 proverb_cluster, 1 wisdom_poem), including spans whose bytes structurally RESIST admonition_unit -- e.g. Prov.24.3 opens בְּ֭חָכְמָה יִבָּ֣נֶה בָּ֑יִת (byte-spliced): no imperative or vetitive form anywhere in the 24:3-4 pair, indicative in both witnesses -- so an exclusive reading would force byte-false structural labels, which a STRUCTURAL vocabulary cannot demand. The controlled-vocabulary reading that holds: admonition_unit is C3's operative category; a C3 row may bear another closed-vocabulary value ONLY where its span's bytes carry no governing second-person imperative/vetitive frame, and must then disclose the deviation from the operative category in device_notes. This APPLIES Section 6 -- the 8-value vocabulary is untouched, both candidate labels are in-vocabulary, no modal is added to or deleted from any line -- and therefore requires no owner referral; the gate rulings are not ambiguous once the section's own modal contrasts are read. (2) THIS row's bytes do not resist the operative category -- they demand it: Prov.22.28 opens אַל תַּ֭סֵּג גְּב֣וּל עוֹלָ֑ם (byte-spliced), a vetitive prohibition (negative particle plus prefix verb; “Don't move the ancient boundary stone which your fathers have set up.” (web:Prov.22.28)), and its opening FOUR words are byte-identical, accents included (re-derived), to the opening four words of Prov.23.10 -- a span this same part correctly types admonition_unit. Identical construction bytes cannot carry two different structural types. The row's own distinguishing ground -- no motive clause, stands alone -- is a span/texture fact, not a type fact: Section 6's '~2-4 vv' is a tilde-marked expectation with no stated minimum (peer_c21's point, confirmed against the section text), so a one-verse bare vetitive is an admonition_unit of span one. The instructive in-cluster contrast is Prov.22.29 (P10-006): חָזִ֡יתָ opens a perfect-verb rhetorical question with no second-person command (its only negative, בַּל יִ֝תְיַצֵּב, is third-person indicative) -- bytes that genuinely stand outside the imperative frame and properly wear single_proverb under the operative-category reading, which is exactly the distinction the mood test preserves. (3) peer_c21's flagged owner PROPOSAL (extending C4's disjunct to comparable atomic C3 verses) is MOOTED for imperative verses like 22:28 by this ruling and unnecessary for non-imperative verses, which the operative-category reading already covers.

consequence.spec: (1) P10-005: unit_type single_proverb -> admonition_unit; span and parent_collection unchanged (Prov.22.28-Prov.22.28, C3). Re-cut rationale/device_notes to argue admonition_unit on its own terms -- a one-verse bare vetitive whose relative clause names the fathers rather than a motive, distinct from the imperative-plus-motive shape of its neighbors -- with the stand-alone character recorded in device_notes as texture, not as a ground for single_proverb. The unit_type change re-opens the dependent fields per the standing rule: rejected_alternative (now rejecting single_proverb on the mood ground), observed_substrate_signals, confidence. (2) peer_c21's cure test is REVISED (boss-over-peer): replace 'unit_type for every C3 row must be a value section 6 grants to C3' with the MOOD TEST -- every C3 row whose span carries a governing second-person imperative/vetitive frame must be typed admonition_unit; a C3 row may bear another closed-vocabulary value only where its span's bytes carry no governing imperative frame, and must disclose the deviation from C3's operative category in device_notes. 'Governing' means the frame structures the span, not merely occurs inside it (an embedded vetitive inside a riddle-anaphora poem does not automatically fire the test) -- argued per row from bytes. (3) Repair-symmetry sweep over the systemic class touched (C3 rows typed on the atomicity/mood conflation): the author wave applies the mood test to the nine remaining non-admonition_unit C3 rows -- P10-006, P10-018, P10-019, P10-021, P10-023, P10-024, P10-025, P10-026, P10-027 -- relabeling where the test fires (Prov.23.23 is the clear second candidate: imperative קְ֭נֵה plus vetitive וְאַל תִּמְכֹּ֑ר, byte-spliced) and verifying-or-installing the deviation disclosure where a non-admonition_unit type legitimately stands (e.g. Prov.22.29 per the bytes in the grounds). Each relabel or retention is argued per row from its own bytes -- no batch verdict; every touched row's prose stays register-clean (no section citations, no positional row references). (4) Queue for book close: a Section 6 clarifying amendment recording the ruled reading (C3 line = operative category; per-bytes typing from the closed vocabulary where the span carries no governing imperative frame, deviation disclosed) -- an owner-facing strategy edit, never row prose. Cure tests: the mood test run over ALL 33 C3 rows must pass (the test that killed the original label); the four-word byte identity between oshb:Prov.22.28 and oshb:Prov.23.10 re-derived and reflected verse-anchored in the re-cut prose; citation_sweep.py, check_universals.py, check_marks.py GREEN on every touched row (the PE at Prov.22.29 stays disclosed single-witness on P10-006 if that row is edited).
